title: बालेनलाई मेन्सन गर्दै भारतीय सांसदको आक्रोश- मोदीले ‘नेपाली आमा’का छोरालाई के गर्दैछन् हेर्नुस्
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौँ । भारतको विपक्षी दल तृणमूल कांग्रेसकी सांसद तथा चर्चित नेता महुआ मोइत्राले नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहलाई मेन्सन गर्दै भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदी र उनको सरकारमाथि तीव्र आक्रोश पोखेकी छन् । प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा प्रधानमन्त्री मोदीले देखाएको आत्मीयताप्रति कटाक्ष गर्दै मोइत्राले भारतकै एक ‘जेन–जी’ युवा नेतालाई बेलायतको अक्सफोर्ड युनियनमा बोल्न जानबाट रोकिएको घटनाप्रति ध्यानाकर्षण गराएकी हुन् । सामाजिक सञ्जाल एक्स (ट्विटर) मा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको आधिकारिक ह्यान्डल (@MahuaMoitra) लाई मेन्सन गर्दै सांसद मोइत्राले लेखेकी छन्- “प्रिय बालेन शाह, एकातिर हाम्रा प्रधानमन्त्री (मोदी) तपाईँसँग नजिकिँदै हुनुहुन्छ भने अर्कोतिर आमा नेपाली मूलको भएकै कारण जेन–जी युवा सौरभ दासलाई अक्सफोर्ड युनियनमा बोल्न जानबाट रोकिएको छ। तपाईँ युवा आन्दोलनको बलमा प्रधानमन्त्री बन्नुभयो। हेर्नुस्, हाम्रा प्रधानमन्त्रीले हाम्रा युवाहरूलाई कस्तो व्यवहार गरिरहेका छन्। लाजमर्दो ! के हो सौरभ दासको प्रकरण? भारतमा युवाहरूको नेतृत्वमा रहेको ‘ककरोच जनता पार्टी’ (सीजेपी) का सह–संयोजक सौरभ दासलाई बेलायतको प्रतिष्ठित अक्सफोर्ड युनिभर्सिटी स्टुडेन्ट्स युनियन (अक्सफोर्ड युनियन) ले एक कार्यक्रममा सम्बोधन गर्न निम्तो दिएको थियो। तर, सोमबार राति लन्डन उड्ने क्रममा दिल्लीस्थित इन्दिरा गान्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलको अध्यागमन काउन्टरमा उनको पासपोर्ट रोक्का गरिएको भन्दै उनलाई विमान चढ्न दिइएन। दासले अक्सफोर्डका साथै क्याम्ब्रिज, लन्डन स्कुल अफ इकोनोमिक्स र एडिनबर्ग विश्वविद्यालयमा समेत आफ्नो आन्दोलनबारे बोल्ने कार्यक्रम तय भएको बताएका छन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा सरकारको आलोचना हुने डरले मोदी सरकारले आफूलाई रोकेको आरोप दास र उनको पार्टीले लगाएको छ। यता, नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन शाह सोमबार मात्रै भारतको औपचारिक भ्रमणका क्रममा नयाँ दिल्लीमा समकक्षी मोदीसँग द्विपक्षीय भेटवार्तामा सहभागी भएका थिए। युवा आन्दोलनको जगबाट उदाएर नेपालको प्रधानमन्त्री बनेका शाहलाई भारतले भव्य स्वागत गरिरहँदा आफ्नै देशका युवा आवाजलाई भने विमानस्थलमै रोकिएको भन्दै सांसद मोइत्राले मोदी सरकारको दोहोरो चरित्रमाथि प्रश्न उठाएकी हुन्। Kathmandu. Mahua Moitra, a prominent leader and MP from India's opposition party Trinamool Congress, has expressed strong anger against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his government, mentioning Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah. Taking a dig at Prime Minister Modi's friendliness during Prime Minister Shah's visit to India, Moitra drew attention to the incident where a 'Gen-G' youth leader from India was prevented from speaking at the Oxford Union in the UK. Mentioning Prime Minister Shah's official handle (2xbzdyaavvil) on social media (Twitter), MP Moitra wrote - "Dear Balen Shah, on one hand our Prime Minister (Modi) is getting closer to you, on the other hand, Gen-G youth Saurabh Das is being prevented from speaking at the Oxford Union because his mother is of Nepali origin. You became the Prime Minister on the strength of the youth movement. Look at how our Prime Minister is treating our youth. Shameful! What is the case of Saurabh Das? Saurabh Das, co-coordinator of the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) in India, was invited to address an event by the prestigious Oxford University Students' Union (Oxford Union) in the UK. However, he was not allowed to board the flight to London on Monday night after his passport was detained at the immigration counter at the Indira Gandhi International Airport in Delhi. Das has said that he is scheduled to speak about his movement at Oxford, as well as Cambridge, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh. Das and his party have accused the Modi government of holding him back for fear of criticism of the government on international forums. Meanwhile, Nepali Prime Minister Balen Shah had a bilateral meeting with his counterpart Modi in New Delhi on Monday during his official visit to India. While India is giving a grand welcome to Shah, who emerged from the youth movement and became Nepal's Prime Minister, MP Moitra has questioned the Modi government's dual character, saying that the youth voices of her own country are being stopped at the airport.

भारतमा युवाहरूको नेतृत्वमा रहेको ‘ककरोच जनता पार्टी’ (सीजेपी) का सह–संयोजक सौरभ दासलाई बेलायतको प्रतिष्ठित अक्सफोर्ड युनिभर्सिटी स्टुडेन्ट्स युनियन (अक्सफोर्ड युनियन) ले एक कार्यक्रममा सम्बोधन गर्न निम्तो दिएको थियो। तर, सोमबार राति लन्डन उड्ने क्रममा दिल्लीस्थित इन्दिरा गान्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलको अध्यागमन काउन्टरमा उनको पासपोर्ट रोक्का गरिएको भन्दै उनलाई विमान चढ्न दिइएन।

दासले अक्सफोर्डका साथै क्याम्ब्रिज, लन्डन स्कुल अफ इकोनोमिक्स र एडिनबर्ग विश्वविद्यालयमा समेत आफ्नो आन्दोलनबारे बोल्ने कार्यक्रम तय भएको बताएका छन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा सरकारको आलोचना हुने डरले मोदी सरकारले आफूलाई रोकेको आरोप दास र उनको पार्टीले लगाएको छ।

यता, नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन शाह सोमबार मात्रै भारतको औपचारिक भ्रमणका क्रममा नयाँ दिल्लीमा समकक्षी मोदीसँग द्विपक्षीय भेटवार्तामा सहभागी भएका थिए। युवा आन्दोलनको जगबाट उदाएर नेपालको प्रधानमन्त्री बनेका शाहलाई भारतले भव्य स्वागत गरिरहँदा आफ्नै देशका युवा आवाजलाई भने विमानस्थलमै रोकिएको भन्दै सांसद मोइत्राले मोदी सरकारको दोहोरो चरित्रमाथि प्रश्न उठाएकी हुन्।

Mahua Moitra, a prominent leader and MP from India's opposition party Trinamool Congress, has expressed strong anger against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his government, mentioning Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah. Taking a dig at Prime Minister Modi's friendliness during Prime Minister Shah's visit to India, Moitra drew attention to the incident where a 'Gen-G' youth leader from India was prevented from speaking at the Oxford Union in the UK. Mentioning Prime Minister Shah's official handle (2xbzdyaavvil) on social media (Twitter), MP Moitra wrote - "Dear Balen Shah, on one hand our Prime Minister (Modi) is getting closer to you, on the other hand, Gen-G youth Saurabh Das is being prevented from speaking at the Oxford Union because his mother is of Nepali origin. You became the Prime Minister on the strength of the youth movement. Look at how our Prime Minister is treating our youth. Shameful! What is the case of Saurabh Das? Saurabh Das, co-coordinator of the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) in India, was invited to address an event by the prestigious Oxford University Students' Union (Oxford Union) in the UK. However, he was not allowed to board the flight to London on Monday night after his passport was detained at the immigration counter at the Indira Gandhi International Airport in Delhi. Das has said that he is scheduled to speak about his movement at Oxford, as well as Cambridge, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh. Das and his party have accused the Modi government of holding him back for fear of criticism of the government on international forums. Meanwhile, Nepali Prime Minister Balen Shah had a bilateral meeting with his counterpart Modi in New Delhi on Monday during his official visit to India. While India is giving a grand welcome to Shah, who emerged from the youth movement and became Nepal's Prime Minister, MP Moitra has questioned the Modi government's dual character, saying that the youth voices of her own country are being stopped at the airport.
